info.title: Tradewinds Age of Sail Economic API
info.description: Headless API for the Tradewinds 17th-18th Century Naval Trading & Financial Simulation

post.summary: Change player passphrase
post.description: Verifies the current passphrase, updates the player's Argon2id passphrase hash, and revokes existing API keys by default (`revoke_all_keys = true`).

400.description: New passphrase fails validation

post.summary: Create scoped API key
post.description: Mints a new scoped API key. Can be authenticated directly with `handle` + `passphrase` in the request body (allowing any scopes and company_id), or delegated via an `Authorization: Bearer` token holding the `account_manage` scope.

400.description: Invalid label, TTL, or empty scopes

401.description: Missing or invalid passphrase / Bearer token

403.description: Requires account_manage scope or attempts privilege escalation

get.description: Lists API keys owned by the authenticated player, optionally filtered by company_id. Company-bound keys can only list keys for their own company.

403.description: Cross-company key enumeration is forbidden

post.summary: Log in with handle and passphrase
post.description: Verifies the player's Argon2id passphrase and issues a revocable, optionally time-limited API key (defaults to 24h TTL and all scopes if omitted).

201.description: Authenticated and session API key issued

post.summary: Revoke API key
post.description: Immediately revokes an active API key. If `key_id` is omitted, revokes the calling Bearer token itself (self-revoke / logout). Revoking another `key_id` requires the `account_manage` scope.

403.description: Requires account_manage scope to revoke another key

post.summary: Revoke all API keys
post.description: Revokes all active API keys for the player (or for a specific company_id), optionally keeping the current calling Bearer key active.

403.description: Requires account_manage scope

get.description: Returns the authenticated player ID, optional bound company ID, granted scopes, and expiration timestamp for the Bearer token.

post.summary: Incorporate a new trading company
post.description: Incorporates a new company at a Phase 1 port, provisions regional banking vaults with starter seed capital, and commissions a starter Hoy berthed with 8t of provisions. Call POST /v1/auth/create-key afterward with the new company_id to mint company-scoped API keys.

400.description: Invalid home port or name

409.description: Company name already taken or company limit reached

post.summary: Declare Admiralty Bankruptcy
post.description: Liquidates remaining company assets and obligations and issues a 250,000p Royal Bankruptcy Bailout Grant plus a fresh Hoy at the home port. Eligible when stranded (no ship, and liquid worth below the cheapest current rebuild quote of a starter hoy, at least 300,000p) or insolvent (liquid worth plus the forced-sale value of every hull beyond one starter hull below 250,000p). Liquid worth: cash in every regional vault (debt negative), escrow the receivership releases, and warehouse and ship cargo valued at the local NPC best bid. One receivership per player per 24 real hours; unpaid futures claims forfeit the grant.

200.description: Admiralty bankruptcy receivership completed and starter ship/bailout granted

409.description: Company is solvent, has ships at sea, or has active contracts/policies

post.summary: Dismiss a Resident Factor
post.description: Dismisses the company's Resident Factor at the specified port, freeing a factor slot and stopping daily salary upkeep.

get.description: Returns the ordered list of port IDs where the company currently maintains a hired Resident Factor.

200.description: List of ports with active Factors

post.summary: Hire a Resident Factor
post.description: Establishes a Resident Factor at the target port for a 75,000p setup fee (and daily salary upkeep). Up to 12 Resident Factors may be active per company.

403.description: Port phase locked

get.description: Returns the company record, owner player handle, active fleet count, ports with hired Resident Factors, and regional banking vault balances.

Returns the company's preferences, with defaults for anything never set: `auto_remit_for_bills` (default true: a daily bill its region's vault cannot cover is topped up by ACH remittance, normal fee, from the other regional vaults, richest first, before the Crown Bailiff acts) and `auto_remit_min_reserve_pence` (default 0: auto-remittance never takes a source vault below this).

patch.description: Partial update: only the fields sent change; unknown fields and an empty body are rejected. Requires the `account_manage` scope, since settings are company-wide policy (auto-remittance moves money between regions on the company's behalf) that narrowly scoped bot keys should not change. Returns the full settings after the update.

400.description: No settings given, unknown field, or a value out of range

403.description: API key lacks the account_manage scope

post.summary: Accept a P2P freight contract and load cargo
post.description: Binds the carrier company to an open freight contract, locks carrier collateral, loads the issuer's cargo onto the berthed ship, and sets a delivery deadline of twice the ship's laden sailing time over the route plus 2 game days.

200.description: Freight contract accepted and cargo loaded

post.summary: Accept a batch of up to 25 P2P freight contracts
post.description: Accepts between 1 and 25 open P2P freight contracts and loads their cargo onto the specified berthed ships. Atomic: if any item fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing item.

200.description: Batch of freight contracts accepted and cargo loaded

post.summary: Post a P2P freight shipping contract
post.description: Locks physical cargo in the issuer's origin warehouse and escrows the freight reward in the regional margin account for a third-party carrier to haul.

post.summary: Deliver cargo toward an Admiralty or Governor charter
post.description: Delivers physical cargo carried in from another port, from a ship berthed at or anchored in the roadstead of the charter port, toward an open Royal Charter or Governor Procurement Charter, earning pence and Crown Prestige (+1 per 1,000p of reward, accrued cumulatively).

200.description: Charter delivery accepted; reward and Crown Prestige credited

400.description: Insufficient cargo or contract already completed

post.summary: Deliver a batch of up to 25 charter fulfillments
post.description: Delivers between 1 and 25 charter cargo installments in a single batch request. Atomic: if any delivery fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing delivery.

400.description: Insufficient cargo or contract already completed

post.summary: Deliver a P2P freight contract at destination
post.description: Unloads contracted cargo from the carrier's ship (berthed or anchored in the destination roadstead) into the issuer's destination warehouse, releasing carrier collateral and paying the escrowed freight reward. If the issuer lacks free leased warehouse space the delivery is refused, the cargo stays aboard and the tender is recorded: should the contract then expire with the carrier still standing by, the issuer is in breach and the carrier is paid.

200.description: Freight cargo delivered; reward paid and collateral released

400.description: Insufficient cargo aboard

409.description: Ship not at the destination port, or issuer has insufficient warehouse space

get.description: Lists charters and P2P freight contracts filtered by type, port, destination, commodity, and status (default `open`), newest first; page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (1-200, default 50). Visibility: public charters (`is_public`: expansion and Admiralty) are listed to everyone, including unauthenticated callers. Other charters (governor procurement, crisis, guild) are listed live only to companies with quay presence (a ship berthed or in the roadstead, or a Resident Factor) at the charter port; open freight only at its origin port; and your own contracts (freight you issued or carry, charters you delivered to) always. Authenticated callers listing open contracts also get gossip copies of non-public charters elsewhere: news reaches your quay ports after 6 game hours plus the sea distance at 5 knots (~1 day across the Channel, ~6 days from the Baltic), and shows the charter as it was when the news left (`stale: true`, `gossip.news_as_of`, `gossip.heard_at_port_id`); it may since have been filled or lapsed. Delivery is first come, first served. Each row is the contract plus typed terms: `remaining_quantity` (tons still to deliver), and for charters `reward_per_ton_pence` (paid per ton delivered), `funded_by` (`crown` or `mint`) and `title`; these are `null` for freight, whose `reward_pence` is paid whole on delivery. `expires_at` is when an open contract lapses.

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description:
Resume after this event id (`0` replays the retained history first); omitted, the stream
delivers only events logged after it opens. Ignored when a `Last-Event-ID` header is sent.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume after this event id (sent automatically by EventSource on reconnect), or `0` to replay the retained history; takes precedence over `after_id`

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each visible StreamEvent is sent with `id:` = event id, `event:` = event_type, `data:` = StreamEvent JSON. Without `Last-Event-ID` or `after_id` only events logged after the stream opens are sent; `0` replays the retained history first. On resume, every visible event logged after `Last-Event-ID` is replayed from the event log (kept 7 days), then the stream goes live with no gaps or duplicates. Control events without an id: `gap` (StreamGap: the resume id is past retention or unknown, events may have been missed, resync via REST, the stream continues live), `auth_revoked` / `auth_expired` (StreamAuthEnded: the API key is no longer valid, the stream ends). Port-scoped events are delivered only for ports where the company has quay-tier visibility (a ship berthed/anchored there or a Resident Factor), at delivery time; the key is re-checked and quay ports refreshed every 30s; keep-alive comments are sent every 15s.

429.description: The company already has the maximum number of open streams (5)

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description:
Return events logged after this event id. `0` replays the retained history from the oldest
event; omitted, the poll starts at the newest event and returns only events logged after
the request.

200.description: Catch-up / long-poll batch of up to `limit` logged events after `after_id` (`after_id=0`: from the oldest retained event; omitted: only events logged after the request), in log order, filtered by company authorization and quay-tier port visibility (ship in port or Resident Factor) as of the request. Waits up to `timeout_ms` when none match. Page forward by passing the last returned id as `after_id`.

410.description: `after_id` is not in the event log (events are kept 7 days) or never existed; events may have been missed, resync via REST

post.summary: Approve a pending convoy join request
post.description: Organizer only, while forming: attaches the requesting ship (still anchored at the origin, not below the minimum speed).

403.description: Not the organizer

409.description: Convoy not forming, ship not ready at origin, or too slow

get.description: Lists convoys the company may see (public ones, and private ones it organizes, was invited to or has a ship in), filtered by id, origin port or status, with route legs, members (hull class, cannons, escort flag, escort fee) and the voyage estimate. The organizer also sees pending join requests and invitees.

post.summary: Organize a new convoy
post.description: Schedules a multi-ship convoy from an anchored flagship's port to a destination port, clearing any berth queue slot on the flagship. Sets who may join (`admission`: open, approval, invite_only), who is told (`visibility`: public, private), an optional minimum speed and an escort fee per ton of a paying joiner's hold.

409.description: Flagship is not anchored in roadstead or is already in a convoy

post.summary: Depart port on a solo voyage
post.description: Plots the shortest unlocked sea route to the destination port and sets sail immediately. Requires turnaround lock to have expired and the ship not to be attached to a convoy. Refused (409 `insufficient_provisions`) when the stores cannot feed the crew to port even without hazards, unless `allow_starvation`; sails but returns a `stores_below_safe` warning when they hold less than the route's `safe_provisions_tons`. Sailing from a berth settles its berth dues (`berth_dues_pence`, `berth_dues_debt_pence`).

409.description: Ship is in turnaround lock, attached to a convoy, or already at sea

post.summary: Detach a ship from a convoy
post.description: Detaches a ship from its convoy while in port, or withdraws its pending join request; any escort fee is refunded. Ships actively sailing at sea cannot detach mid-voyage.

409.description: Cannot detach ship while actively sailing at sea

post.summary: Dock an anchored ship at a port berth
post.description: Moves a ship from offshore roadstead into a physical berth (or queues it if all of the port's effective berths are occupied within their protected window). Berthing is free, but berth dues accrue per game day berthed (`berth_dues_per_day_pence`, rising with occupancy; at least 6 game hours a stay) and are settled from the owner's vault in the port's banking region when the ship leaves the berth (offshore, depart, eviction) and daily in the upkeep pass; dues a vault cannot cover are booked as vault debt (collected by the bailiff). The roadstead is free. Ships attached to a convoy must detach first.

409.description: Ship is attached to a convoy, at sea, or not in roadstead

post.summary: Fund a Crown Naval Patrol in a sea zone
post.description: Suppresses `suppressed_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) of a sea zone's piracy for `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440), paying the Crown 2 Crowns per bps per game day of the term (at least 100 Crowns) from the home regional vault; `cost_pence` in the response is what was paid. Contributions from every company stack, capped at 5,000 bps per zone. The sponsor is anonymous: the public `naval_patrol_funded` notice and `GET /v1/world/zones` show only the zone's totals.

400.description: Insufficient funds

post.summary: Invite a company to a forming convoy
post.description: Organizer only: the invited company's ships join without approval (even an invite-only convoy) and it sees the convoy if private.

403.description: Not the organizer

post.summary: Sponsor a Letter of Marque in a sea zone
post.description: Adds `added_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) to a sea zone's piracy for `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440), paying the Crown 2 Crowns per bps per game day of the term (at least 100 Crowns) from the home regional vault; `cost_pence` in the response is what was paid. Contributions from every company stack, capped at 5,000 bps per zone. While it is in force the sponsor earns prize money from every pirate interception in the zone: the prize court pays half the seized cargo's base value, times the marques' share of the zone's piracy (marque bps over base + marque bps, patrols ignored), split among the marques in force pro rata by bps, from the world mint into the vault of the region the bounty was paid from (ledger reason `letter_of_marque_prize`, a private `marque_prize_paid` event naming the marque, zone, amount and goods, never the ship or its owner). The sponsor is anonymous: the public `letter_of_marque_issued` notice and `GET /v1/world/zones` show only the zone's totals, and the victim's events never name it.

201.description: Letter of Marque issued to privateers

400.description: Insufficient funds

post.summary: Join a forming convoy
post.description: Asks to put a ship anchored at the convoy's origin port into a forming convoy (optionally as an escort, if it mounts cannons). It joins at once (`joined`) if the convoy is open, the company is invited or organizes it; on an approval convoy it waits (`pending`) for the organizer. Any escort fee is escrowed now.

200.description: Ship joined convoy or request pending

403.description: Convoy admits invited companies only

409.description: Convoy already departed, ship not anchored at origin, already in a convoy, or would hold the convoy below its minimum speed

post.summary: Remove another company's ship from a forming convoy
post.description: Organizer only, before departure: detaches the ship and refunds its escort fee.

403.description: Not the organizer

409.description: Convoy not forming, or the ship is the organizer's own

get.summary: List company's sponsored Letters of Marque
get.description: Returns the Letters of Marque the authenticated company sponsored (active and historical), newest first, each with the prize money it has earned so far (`prize_earned_pence`) and the region it is paid into (`banking_region`). Paginated by `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (default 100, at most 500). Sponsors are anonymous: other companies' marques are never listed; each zone's live totals are public at `GET /v1/world/zones`.

post.summary: Move a ship to offshore roadstead anchorage
post.description: Vacates a physical port berth (once turnaround lock has elapsed) or cancels a berth queue reservation, anchoring the vessel in the offshore roadstead. Leaving a berth settles its berth dues (`berth_dues_pence`, of which `berth_dues_debt_pence` booked as vault debt); the roadstead accrues none, so an idle ship can wait there.

409.description: Ship is still inside its physical turnaround lock or at sea

get.summary: List company's funded Crown Naval Patrols
get.description: Returns the Crown Naval Patrols the authenticated company funded (active and historical), newest first. Sponsors are anonymous: other companies' patrols are never listed; each zone's live totals are public at `GET /v1/world/zones`.

post.summary: Move provisions into a ship's stores
post.description: Moves provisions into the ship's stores, which its crew eats (per leg at sea, and in port at half the sea rate, a ton per 200 crew-days: `port_provisions_tons_per_day` on GET /v1/world/route): from its own cargo (`source: cargo`, berthed or in the roadstead; sealed freight is never touched) or from the company's warehouse at the berth (`source: warehouse`; needs free cargo space, since stores take hold space, and extends the stevedore turnaround). To buy provisions straight into the stores, place an IOC bid with `into_stores: true` on POST /v1/market/order.

400.description: Not enough provisions at the source, or no hold space

403.description: Ship not berthed (warehouse) or not at port (cargo)

post.summary: Reject a pending convoy join request
post.description: Organizer only, while forming: turns the request down and refunds its escort fee.

403.description: Not the organizer

get.description: Returns full status, berth lock timestamps, cargo manifest, stores, and route legs for a single company vessel.
Returns the company's vessels with effective cargo capacity (hold less cannons and stores), cargo manifest, stores (provisions the crew eats), and active route legs.

post.summary: Take provisions out of a ship's stores
post.description: Moves provisions out of the ship's stores into its cargo (`destination: cargo`, berthed or in the roadstead; they count as loaded at this port, so they cannot fill a charter here) or into the company's warehouse at the berth (`destination: warehouse`; needs free leased space and extends the stevedore turnaround). Stores must be moved to cargo before they can be sold or delivered.

400.description: Not enough provisions in the stores, or no warehouse space

403.description: Ship not berthed (warehouse) or not at port (cargo)

post.summary: Accept an open commodity futures order
post.description: Takes the opposite side of an open physical commodity futures contract at a regional hub port, locking 25% counterparty margin and activating the contract until maturity.

400.description: Futures order not open or insufficient margin

post.summary: Accept a batch of up to 25 open futures orders
post.description: Matches and activates between 1 and 25 open physical commodity futures contracts. Atomic: if any item fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing futures_id.

200.description: Batch of futures orders matched and activated

400.description: Futures order not open or insufficient margin

post.summary: Create a physical commodity futures order
post.description: Posts a standardized physical commodity futures bid or ask at a regional hub port, locking 25% initial margin in the company's regional margin escrow account.

201.description: Standardized commodity futures order created with 25% margin locked

400.description: Port is not a regional hub or insufficient margin funds

post.summary: Create a batch of up to 25 futures orders
post.description: Posts between 1 and 25 physical commodity futures orders at regional hub ports. Atomic: if any order fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing order.

201.description: Batch of standardized commodity futures orders created

400.description: Port is not a regional hub or insufficient margin funds

get.description: Lists open, active, settled, and defaulted physical commodity futures contracts at regional hub ports.

200.description: List of standardized physical commodity futures

post.summary: Settle a matured commodity futures contract
post.description: Executes physical delivery or Admiralty default settlement for a futures contract that has reached its maturity timestamp, ahead of the scheduled `FuturesSettlement` job. Only the contract's buyer or seller may call it; anyone else gets `403`. Idempotent if already settled.

200.description: Matured futures contract settled or defaulted

400.description: Futures contract has not reached maturity yet

403.description: The calling company is neither the buyer nor the seller

post.summary: Request a Lloyd's marine insurance policy for a ship voyage
post.description: Creates an open marine insurance policy for a vessel in port, escrowing the total premium in the company's regional margin account for underwriters to cover.

201.description: Marine insurance policy created; total premium escrowed

400.description: Invalid premium bps, ship not in port, or insufficient funds

get.description: Lists marine insurance policies across all ports, newest first. Filter by `status`, `origin_port_id`, `dest_port_id`, `ship_id`, `insured_company_id` (the shipowner who took the policy out) and `underwriter_company_id` (a company holding a slice); pass your own company id to either to see your policies. Page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (1-200, default 50).

parameters.name: insured_company_id
parameters.description: Only policies this company took out (the insured shipowner).

parameters.name: underwriter_company_id
parameters.description: Only policies this company underwrote a slice of.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Page backwards from this policy id (the last `id` of the previous page).

200.description: List of Lloyd's of London marine insurance policies

post.summary: Underwrite a slice of a marine insurance policy
post.description: Pledges collateral for a basis-point slice (minimum 500 bps, in 100 bps increments) of an open or active marine insurance policy.

200.description: Policy slice underwritten; collateral locked in margin escrow

400.description: Invalid slice bps, self-underwriting, or insufficient funds

post.summary: Underwrite a batch of up to 25 marine insurance policy slices
post.description: Underwrites between 1 and 25 marine insurance policy slices in a single batch request. Atomic: if any item fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing item.

400.description: Invalid slice bps, self-underwriting, or insufficient funds

get.summary: Get port limit order book (cut to your visibility tier)
get.description: Returns a port's books cut to the company's `visibility` tier there. `storage` (any warehouse lease): best bid/ask from the once-per-game-day snapshot, `as_of` = snapshot time. `counting_house` (lease >= 5% of the port's warehouse capacity): live best bid/ask, `as_of` = now. `quay` (ship berthed/anchored at the port or a Resident Factor): live best bid/ask plus `depth` (every resting order, NPC stockpile, equilibrium mid-price). `depth` is `null` below quay.

200.description: Port order books at the company's visibility tier

403.description: No lease, ship or factor at this port (no_port_presence)

post.summary: Cancel a resting limit order
post.description: Cancels an open GTC limit order owned by the company and immediately releases any locked margin escrow or warehouse inventory.

post.summary: Cancel a batch of up to 50 resting orders
post.description: Cancels between 1 and 50 open GTC limit orders owned by the company and unlocks their escrowed funds or inventory. Atomic: if any cancel fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing order_id.

200.description: Batch of orders cancelled and collateral unlocked

get.description: Lists historical trade executions where the authenticated company acted as either maker or taker.
Lists the authenticated company's open resting GTC limit orders across all ports, with optional port, commodity, side, and cursor pagination filters.

post.summary: Place a spot or resting limit order
post.description: Submits an IOC or GTC limit order to a port's central limit order book. Matches immediately against opposing liquidity in price-time priority and optionally posts any unfilled remainder as a resting GTC order.

200.description: Order matched and/or placed on book

403.description: No lease, ship or factor at the order port (no_port_presence), or missing scope

post.summary: Place a batch of up to 25 orders
post.description: Submits between 1 and 25 spot or resting limit orders in one transaction (grouped by port and commodity, request order kept within a book). Atomic: if any order fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing order.

200.description: Batch of orders matched and/or placed on book

403.description: No lease, ship or factor at the order port (no_port_presence), or missing scope

get.description: Returns the authenticated player's account record along with all maritime trading companies owned by the player.

post.summary: Register player account
post.description: Creates a new player account secured with an Argon2id passphrase hash. The handle is `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{3,32}` and unique case-insensitively (`Drake` and `drake` are the same handle; login accepts either). No initial API key is issued on registration; call POST /v1/auth/create-key or POST /v1/auth/login with your passphrase to mint scoped API keys.

400.description: Invalid handle or passphrase

post.summary: Commission a new ship at a shipyard
post.description: Constructs a new vessel at a shipyard port using either Bring-Your-Own-Materials (BYOM) from the company's warehouse or Turnkey Cash priced off local stockpile equilibrium.

400.description: Port lacks shipyard or insufficient materials/funds

post.summary: Modify a berthed ship's cannon armament at a shipyard
post.description: Reconfigures a berthed ship's cannon armament (2t hold per cannon). Mounting additional cannons requires a shipyard port and costs 150 Crowns (15,000 pence) per added cannon.

400.description: Invalid cannon count, insufficient hold space, or not berthed at a shipyard port

get.summary: Quote the exact cost of a ship build
get.description: Prices a build exactly as POST /v1/shipyard/build-ship would charge it right now, using the same pricing function: shipwright labour, and for `turnkey_cash` each material walked up the port's NPC ask ladder plus the 15% yard markup. `in_stock` per material (turnkey: the yard's stockpile; BYOM: your unlocked warehouse stock here) and `available` say whether the build can go ahead; `total_cost_pence` is null when a turnkey material cannot be supplied. Needs the same presence at the port as building; the quote holds no stock, so it matches the charge only while the book does not move.

400.description: Port has no shipyard

403.description: Port or ship class phase locked, or no presence at the port

get.description: Returns double-entry ledger entries affecting the company's accounts, ordered newest first, with optional filtering by banking region, reason, and UUIDv7 cursor.
Computes the live basis-point fee matrix for wiring funds between every pair of regional clearinghouses based on net clearing flow imbalances.

200.description: Live inter-regional ACH remittance fee matrix

post.summary: Wire funds between regional vaults (ACH)
post.description: Executes an instant inter-regional ACH wire transfer between two of the company's regional vaults, deducting the dynamic clearinghouse basis-point fee.

400.description: Insufficient funds or invalid amount

403.description: Missing treasury_remit scope

get.description: Returns all regional banking vaults and derivatives margin escrow accounts owned by the company across all banking regions.
Returns the company's leased, reserved, used, and free warehouse tonnage along with stored commodities at a single port.
Returns warehouse lease capacity, reserved tonnage, used tonnage, and commodity inventory across all ports where the company has active presence or inventory.

post.summary: Load cargo from warehouse onto ship
post.description: Transfers one or more unlocked commodity stacks from the port warehouse into a berthed ship's hold and extends the ship's stevedore turnaround lock.

400.description: Insufficient hold space or unlocked warehouse stock

403.description: Ship not berthed

post.summary: Set port warehouse lease tonnage
post.description: Adjusts the company's leased warehouse capacity at a port. Increasing lease requires existing presence at the port (a ship berthed/anchored there, a Resident Factor, or an existing lease) and available port warehouse capacity; a lease of at least 5% of the port's capacity upgrades visibility to counting-house (live top of book); decreasing lease cannot drop below used + reserved tonnage.

403.description: No presence at the port when increasing lease (no_port_presence)

409.description: Port capacity exceeded or target below used + reserved tonnage

post.summary: Unload cargo from ship into warehouse
post.description: Transfers one or more commodity stacks from a berthed ship's hold into free leased port warehouse space and extends the ship's stevedore turnaround lock.

400.description: Insufficient free leased warehouse space or ship cargo

403.description: Ship not berthed

get.description: Returns all commodities (with reference base prices and recipes), ship classes, sea zones, and ports across all 4 expansion phases. Each port lists its live customs rate and the goods it currently produces, manufactures and imports in this world: what it trades, never how much (market sizes and rates are rolled per world and drift).

get.summary: Get current game clock and calendar state
get.description: Returns the current real-world UTC timestamp, season number, unlocked phase, global health score, 24h player trading volume, whether the world is paused, `season_planned_end_at` (the season end the operators announced; `null` until announced; the season is ended by hand on that date, never automatically) and the in-game calendar date.

200.description: Current game clock and calendar state

get.description: What anyone may see of a company, by exact name: `company_name`, `home_port_id`, `founded_at`, its `leaderboard_rank` when it is a player's ranked company in the top 20, and the hall-of-fame `titles` its owner earned in past seasons (shown on the owner's flagship company only: its leaderboard entry, else its oldest company that has not been bankrupt). Nothing else: no owner, balances, fleet or sponsorships.

get.summary: List world events, active or historical
get.description: Returns world events newest first: the director's macro shocks (`supply_boom`, `demand_shortage`, `admiralty_mobilization`, `pirate_outbreak`) and structural shifts (`structural: true`: `production_collapse`, `production_boom`, `import_slump`). By default only events still in effect; `include_expired=true` returns the world's full history (never pruned). Filter by `event_type`, `structural`, `port_id` and `since` (start time); page with `cursor` (the last id of the previous page) and `limit` (default 50, max 200). Events say what happened where, never by how much or for how long.

parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description:
Also return events that have lapsed (the world's history). Default `false`: only events
still in effect.

parameters.name: structural
parameters.description: `true`: only structural shifts; `false`: only the director's macro shocks.

parameters.name: port_id
parameters.description: Only events at this port (sea-zone events such as `pirate_outbreak` have none).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events that started at or after this instant.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Return events older than this event id (the last id of the previous page).

get.summary: Theatre progression: expansion tier progress and contribution leaderboards
get.description: Returns the world's `unlocked_phase`, the Admiralty expansion tier now open (each open charter's tons required/delivered/remaining, progress, current rate, escalations, `expires_at` and game hours left; the tier's tons delivered and remaining and its completion bonus pool) and every completed tier. Each tier lists its contributors by company name with the tons they delivered and their share of the tier (`share_bps`, which is also their share of the completion bonus). Public: no company ids, balances or payouts.

get.summary: Hall of fame: past seasons' top players
get.description: Every ended season, newest first, with its top 10 players by final rank (each player ranked by their best company: `company_name`, `home_port_id`, `net_worth_pence`) and the cosmetic `title` the top 3 earned (`Season <n> Champion`, `Season <n> Master Mariner`). The archive survives world wipes; titles show on the winner's flagship company in later seasons and have no gameplay effect.

get.summary: Season leaderboard: top 20 players by their best company's net worth
get.description: The live season leaderboard, recomputed every real hour (`refreshed_at`, `next_refresh_at`), never per request. Players rank by their **best** company only: one entry per player, naming that company (`company_name`, `home_port_id`), its `net_worth_pence` (cash and escrow in every region, goods owned at catalog base prices, hulls afloat at build value: the same figure the season archive records) and any hall-of-fame `titles` its owner won in past seasons. A company that went through Admiralty bankruptcy never ranks again; its player's other or new companies can. Top 20 only, no player handles or ids; marque and patrol sponsorship is never shown. With a company key, `you` is your player's own rank (also outside the top 20) and which of your companies holds it.

200.description: Top players and the caller's own rank

get.summary: Get port details, your visibility tier, and Coffee House gossip board
get.description: Returns public port metrics (customs rate, health score, berth occupancy, dock queue, warehouse capacity and the lease needed for a counting-house), the authenticated company's `visibility` tier here (`none`, `storage`, `counting_house`, `quay`), and, at `quay` tier only (a ship berthed/anchored here or a Resident Factor), the Coffee House gossip board with per-report `snapshot_at`/`age_seconds` and `recent_sailings`: ships seen sailing from or entering the port in the last 24 game hours (name, hull class, owner, bound for / came from, convoy, and `load_state` `ballast` <10% / `part_laden` / `laden` >70% of hold; never cargo, stores or timings).

get.summary: List ports with optional phase and banking region filters
get.description: Returns the catalog entries of ports (as in `/v1/world/catalog`) filtered by maximum expansion phase and/or banking region.

get.summary: Plan shortest maritime route between two ports
get.description: Computes the shortest sea-zone path between two ports within `max_phase` (default: the world's current `unlocked_phase`), returning individual route legs, total distance in nautical miles, and the provisions the stores need: crews eat exactly one ton per 100 crew-days at sea and stores are kept exactly (fractional tons), so `expected_provisions_tons` is what is eaten before the last leg sets out (no hazards) and `safe_provisions_tons` also survives one storm or pirate hit taking 25% of the stores. Buy the shortfall against the ship's `stores.provisions_tons`, rounded up to whole tons.

200.description: Shortest maritime route and provisions estimate

404.description: No valid route within unlocked phase

get.summary: Live piracy of every sea zone
get.description: Returns each sea zone's catalog `base_piracy_bps`, the summed piracy of the letters of marque in force (`marque_piracy_bps`, player-sponsored, corsair flotillas and mutineers alike) and the suppression of the Crown Naval Patrols in force (`patrol_suppression_bps`), each capped at 5,000 bps, with their counts and soonest expiry, and `net_piracy_bps` = max(0, base + marque - patrol): what every ship sailing the zone faces and what Lloyd's prices. Contributions from all companies stack. Aggregates only: sponsors are never named.

carrier_ship_id.description: The ship now carrying (and bound to deliver) the cargo.

collateral_pence.description: Escrowed from the carrier; returned on delivery, forfeit on default.

delivery_deadline.description: Deliver at `dest_port_id` before this, or the contract defaults.

AccountType.description:
Classification of a double-entry ledger account within a [`BankingRegion`].

All account balances are denominated in [`Pence`] (`100 pence = 1 Crown`).

oneOf.description:
Turnkey: what the yard pays for `quantity` walking the port's NPC ask ladder (before the
yard markup); `null` if the yard cannot supply it. BYOM: `null` (you supply it).

in_stock.description:
Turnkey: the yard's stockpile holds `quantity`. BYOM: your warehouse here holds `quantity`
unlocked.

BuildMode.description: Construction payment and material sourcing mode for shipyard orders.

BuildQuoteResult.description: Exact price of a build right now (`GET /v1/shipyard/quote`).

available.description: Every material is in stock, so the build can go ahead now (funds permitting).

labour_pence.description: Shipwright labour, charged in every mode.

materials_pence.description: Turnkey: sum of the materials' `cost_pence`. BYOM: 0.

oneOf.description:
`labour + materials + markup`: what `POST /v1/shipyard/build-ship` would charge now, from
the port region's vault. `null` when a turnkey material cannot be supplied.

CargoManifest.description:
Map of commodity quantities (in metric `tons`) currently loaded in a ship's cargo hold.

Invariant: all stored values are strictly positive (`> 0`); zeroed entries are removed automatically.

propertyNames.description: Validated canonical commodity identifier (`"provisions"`, `"grain"`, etc.) backed by the static commodity catalog.

CharterFunding.description: Which world account pays a charter's deliveries (`metadata.funded_by`, set at posting).

CharterGossip.description:
How a non-public charter elsewhere reached the viewer: coffee-house news carried by passing
ships, delayed by sea distance (see `crate::math::charter_news_delay`).

heard_at_port_id.description: The viewer's quay port where the news arrived first.

news_as_of.description: When the news left the charter's port: the listing shows the charter as it was then.

CommodityDepthResult.description:
Full live depth and NPC stockpile of one book; only revealed at quay-tier visibility.

`npc_current_stock` is what a sailor on the quay can see in the port's warehouses (the NPC ask
ladder already reveals it: each ask tranche is a tenth of the stock). The port's normal stock
level and its production and consumption rates are never published: they are rolled per world
and drift, and must be inferred from how prices move.

CommodityId.description: Validated canonical commodity identifier (`"provisions"`, `"grain"`, etc.) backed by the static commodity catalog.

oneOf.description: Best ask as of the response's `as_of` (`null` when that side was empty).
Best bid as of the response's `as_of` (`null` when that side was empty).
Full depth and stockpile; `null` below quay-tier visibility.

CompanySettings.description:
User-set company preferences (`GET`/`PATCH /v1/company/settings`). A company that never set
anything gets [`CompanySettings::default`]; each new preference is a new field with a default
(and a defaulted `company_settings` column), so older rows keep working unchanged.

auto_remit_for_bills.description:
When a daily bill (warehouse rent, fleet/factor upkeep) is due in a region whose vault
cannot cover it, top that vault up by ACH remittance (normal fee) from the company's
other regional vaults, richest first, before the Crown Bailiff is called. Off: bills are
paid from the billing region's vault only. Default `true`.

auto_remit_min_reserve_pence.description: Auto-remittance never takes a source vault below this balance (pence). Default `0`.

is_public.description:
Listed to everyone (expansion and Admiralty charters). Otherwise seen only with quay
presence at its port (charters: the delivery port; freight: the origin), by its parties,
and (charters) as delayed coffee-house gossip in other ports.

oneOf.description: Charters: which world account pays deliveries. Freight: `null` (the issuer escrowed it).
Where and as of when a gossiped charter was heard; `null` for a live listing.

Charters: pence paid per ton delivered. Freight: `null` (its `reward_pence` is paid whole
on delivery).

stale.description:
`true` for a gossiped copy: `remaining_quantity`, `quantity_delivered` and `status` are as
the news stood at `gossip.news_as_of`; the charter may since have been filled or lapsed.

title.description: Charter title, if it has one.

ContractListing.description: A listed contract with its terms typed out; `contract.metadata` keeps the raw record.

ContractStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a freight or charter contract.

ContractType.description: Category of maritime commercial contract on the contract board.

escort_fee_pence_per_ton.description: Escort fee per ton of a paying member's hold capacity (`0`: none).

min_speed_centiknots.description: Joiners that would hold the convoy below this speed are refused.

ConvoyAdmission.description: Who may join a forming convoy.

ConvoyMemberInfo.description:
A ship in (or asking to join) a convoy, as every party sees it: its hull is public, and what
Lloyd's prices the convoy discount on.

escort_fee_pence.description: Escort fee escrowed for this ship (`0` for escorts and the organizer's ships).

hull_category.description:
Water the hull is rated for (`coastal` < `regional` < `oceanic`): consorts rated for a
zone can rescue a member there.

is_escort.description: Escorts pay no escort fee and share the fees paid, pro rata to cannons, on arrival.

escort_fee_pence.description: Escort fee escrowed for the ship (on join or request) or refunded (on leaving).

estimated_arrival_at.description:
The convoy's estimated arrival with its membership after this change (`null` when it has
no members left or is no longer forming/sailing).

status.description:
`joined`, `pending` (awaiting the organizer), `approved`, `rejected`, `kicked`, `detached`
or `withdrawn` (a pending request taken back).

invited_company_ids.description: Companies invited: shown to the organizer only (empty for others).

members.description: Members (joined while forming; sailing, arrived or lost after departure).

pending_requests.description: Join requests awaiting approval: shown to the organizer only (empty for others).

oneOf.description:
Estimated schedule at the convoy's current speed (its slowest member's): from
`convoy.departs_at` with the ships mustered so far while forming, from the leg under way
while sailing; `null` once arrived or cancelled, or while it has no members.

ConvoyStatus.description: Operational lifecycle state of a multi-ship convoy.

ConvoyVisibility.description: Who is told about a convoy and sees it listed.

depart_in_game_minutes.description: Muster window in game minutes, clamped to [`MIN_CONVOY_MUSTER`]..=[`MAX_CONVOY_MUSTER`].

escort_fee_pence_per_ton.description:
Escort fee per ton of a paying joiner's hold capacity (`0..=MAX_ESCORT_FEE_PENCE_PER_TON`,
default `0`).

min_speed_centiknots.description:
Refuse joiners that would hold the convoy below this speed; at departure, other companies'
slowest ships are left behind until it is met.

visibility.description: `private` convoys are announced and listed only to invitees and members (default `public`).

matures_in_game_hours.description: Time to maturity in game hours (default `30`, clamped to `1..=1440`).

bailout_capital_pence.description: The grant's bailout capital; `0` when it was withheld.

claims_paid_pence.description: Futures default claims owed to counterparties paid from the company's cash first.

claims_written_off_pence.description:
Futures default claims the cash could not cover: written off, never minted to the creditor.
Any write-off withholds the Royal grant.

cooldown_until.description: When this player's companies may next declare bankruptcy.

new_ship_id.description: The fresh hoy of the Royal grant; `None` when the grant was withheld.

ship_id.description:
Ship delivering the goods, berthed at or anchored in the roadstead of the charter port.
Only cargo it carried in from another port is accepted; goods bought or loaded at the
charter port since arrival are not.

allow_starvation.description:
Sail even though the crew would run out of provisions in the ship's stores before arrival
(half speed, a fifth of the cargo spoiled per unfed leg, a 50% mutiny roll per unfed leg
after the first). Provisions carried as cargo do not count. Without it such a departure is
refused with `409 insufficient_provisions`.

berth_dues_debt_pence.description: The part of `berth_dues_pence` booked as vault debt.

berth_dues_pence.description: Berth dues settled on leaving the berth (0 when it sailed from the roadstead).

first_leg_arrives_at.description: When the first leg ends (scheduled exactly).

legs.description: Per-leg estimated arrivals; the first equals `first_leg_arrives_at`.

warnings.description: Risks the ship sailed with anyway (empty when none): see [`DepartWarning`].

DepartWarning.description: A risk `depart` accepted rather than refused.

buy_tons.description: Whole tons to buy into the stores to reach `safe_tons` (rounded up).

code.description:
`stores_below_safe`: the stores hold less than the route's `safe_provisions_tons`, so one
storm or pirate hit (each takes a quarter of the stores) can leave the crew unfed before
port, and a starving crew may mutiny, which no insurance pays for.

have_tons.description: Provisions in the stores at departure (tons, fractional).

required_tons.description:
Least the stores must hold (tons, fractional) to reach port fed with this cargo and no
hazards.

safe_tons.description: The route's `safe_provisions_tons` (survives one hazard on any leg).

oneOf.description:
The part of `berth_dues_pence` the owner's vault in the port's region could not cover,
booked as vault debt (the bailiff collects it).
Berth dues settled because this call took the ship out of its berth (`offshore`).

The port's berth dues per game day at the occupancy when this call berthed the ship (only
when it did). Dues accrue while berthed and are settled on leaving the berth and daily.

ExpansionCharterProgress.description:
One charter of the tier in play (open, or completed: full), as `GET /v1/world/expansion` shows
it.

beyond_coastal_water.description:
The port lies beyond coastal water from every company home: a starter hoy cannot reach it
over rated water.

escalations.description: Times this charter was re-posted after a stalled window, each raising its rate.

game_hours_left.description: Game hours until it lapses (and is re-posted).

premium_bps.description:
The charter's premium over the good's catalog base price, in bps (the highest of the tier
beyond the starter hull's rated water).

progress_bps.description: Delivered share of this charter's cap, in bps.

quantity_required.description: The charter's cap: it stops accepting once this much is delivered.

status.description: `open`, or `completed` once full (it then takes no more deliveries).

tons_delivered_total.description:
Tons delivered for this good at this port across the charter's re-posts: its contribution
to the tier's combined `tons_delivered`.

ExpansionContributor.description: One company's public standing on a tier's contribution leaderboard.

share_bps.description:
Share of the tier's contribution (tons valued at the tier's base rates), in bps: also the
share of the completion bonus.

tons.description: Tons delivered against the tier's charters.

active_trading_companies.description:
Companies that traded within the last 7 game days or have a ship at sea now (NPC houses
excluded): what the tier in play is sized for, recomputed every world-director tick.

oneOf.description: The tier now open (targeting `unlocked_phase + 1`; `null` once Phase 4 is open).

ExpansionTierStatus.description: One expansion tier's progress and contribution leaderboard.

active_companies.description: Active trading companies when the target was last recomputed.

charter_capacity_tons.description:
Tons the open charters still accept, combined (more than `tons_remaining`: no single
charter is required).

charters.description: The tier's charters (the tier in play only): open ones and full ones.

completion_bonus_pence.description: Split among the contributors pro rata by `share_bps` when the tier completes.

target_tons.description:
The tier's target tonnage: `tons_per_company` per active trading company, at least
`min_tons` (as last sized, see `active_companies`).

tons_delivered.description:
Tons delivered against the tier so far, across all its charters: the tier completes when
this reaches `target_tons`.

duration_game_hours.description:
Term in game hours (default `60`, clamped to `5..=1440`). The price is
`2 Cr` per bps per game day of it ([`crate::math::zone_intervention_cost_pence`]).

suppressed_piracy_bps.description: Piracy the patrol suppresses in the zone (bps, clamped to `50..=1500`).

FuturesStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a forward commodity futures contract.

GameCalendarDate.description: Snapshot of the 18th-century in-game calendar derived from the real-time [`WorldClock`].

time_scale.description: Active simulation time scale multiplier (e.g. `60` = 60 game seconds per 1 real second).

total_game_hours.description: Cumulative in-game hours elapsed since `season_epoch` (world time, from 1 March 1700).

GossipCommodityReport.description:
Delayed market intelligence carried by ships from a distant port: what a sailor saw on that
port's quay as of `snapshot_at` (warehouse stock in metric `tons`, best bid and best ask in
pence per ton, `null` when that side of the book was empty).

company_name.description: The player's ranked company that season.

top.description: The season's top [`HALL_OF_FAME_PLAYERS`] players, by final player rank.

HallOfFameTitle.description: A cosmetic hall-of-fame title earned in a past season.

player_rank.description: The player's final rank that season.

InsurableValueExceeded.description: Why a policy was refused for insuring more than the ship is worth.

hull_value_pence.description: The hull rebuild quote within that maximum.

max_insurable_pence.description: The most the ship can be insured for: its hull rebuild quote plus its current cargo.

requested_pence.description: The sum insured that was requested.

hull_value_pence.description:
The hull's insurable value when the policy was written (its rebuild quote then, see
`shipyard::rebuild_value_pence`); the sum insured above it is the declared cargo.

InsuranceStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a maritime hull insurance policy.

added_piracy_bps.description: Piracy the privateers add in the zone (bps, clamped to `50..=1500`).

duration_game_hours.description:
Term in game hours (default `60`, clamped to `5..=1440`). The price is
`2 Cr` per bps per game day of it ([`crate::math::zone_intervention_cost_pence`]).

as_escort.description: Join as an escort (the ship needs cannons): pays no fee, shares the fees on arrival.

rank.description: The player's rank (players rank by their best company).

titles.description: Hall-of-fame titles the company's owner earned in past seasons (cosmetic).

LeaderboardOwnRank.description: The calling company's player's own standing.

company_name.description: The player's ranked (best) company: the caller, or another of the player's companies.

is_calling_company.description: The caller is the player's ranked company.

next_refresh_at.description: When the next hourly refresh is due.

refreshed_at.description: When the snapshot was computed (`null` before the first refresh of the season).

oneOf.description:
With a company key: the caller's player's rank (also when outside the top 20); `null`
without a key or when the player has no rankable company in the snapshot.

LegEstimate.description: Estimated arrival at the end of one route leg.

speed_centiknots.description: Speed the leg is (or is expected to be) sailed at.

starving.description:
A ship sets out on this leg with no provisions in its stores: it sails at half speed,
spoils a fifth of its cargo and, from the second leg of the route on, risks a 50% mutiny.

oneOf.description:
The region whose vault paid the bounty, where prize money is paid (`None` for a corsair
flotilla or a mutiny's marque, whose prize share nobody is paid).

cost_pence.description: What the sponsor paid the Crown (`0` for a corsair flotilla or a mutiny's marque).

prize_earned_pence.description:
Prize money paid to the sponsor so far: its pro rata share (by bps) of the marques' share of
every pirate interception in the zone while it is in force, at
[`MARQUE_PRIZE_COURT_BPS`](crate::math::MARQUE_PRIZE_COURT_BPS) of the seized cargo's base value.

LoadState.description: How deep a ship sits in the water, as seen from the quay.

cost_pence.description: What the sponsor paid the Crown.

NonNegativeTons.description:
Non-negative physical tonnage in tons, bounded to `0..=MAX_TONS`.

Used for target lease capacities and inventory levels where zero is valid but negative values are not.

OrderSide.description: Side of an order on the Central Limit Order Book (CLOB).

Pence.description:
Signed monetary amount denominated in pence (`100 pence = 1 Crown`).

Used for account balances, PnL calculations, and net clearing flows where zero or negative values
may appear in intermediate calculations.

into_stores.description:
Buy straight into the ship's stores (what its crew eats) instead of its cargo. Only for an
IOC bid for `provisions` with `ship_id` set; stores take hold space like cargo.

PortCatalogEntry.description:
A port as this world knows it: fixed geography and facilities, its live customs rate, and the
goods it currently trades by role. Says *what* a port trades, never how much: stock levels and
production or consumption rates are rolled per world and drift, so they must be scouted.

customs_bps.description:
Live customs rate (bps) an importer pays per buy fill here; rolled per world, then eased by
distress or quiet trade (see `GET /v1/world/port`).

effective_berths.description:
Berths now: grows above `base_berths` with the active fleet (`max(base, round(base *
sqrt(active_ships / 40)))`, recomputed every port macro tick).

manufactures.description: Goods its workshops make (from inputs it must have on hand).

berth_dues_per_day_pence.description:
Harbour dues per game day berthed at the occupancy now: 10 Cr a day in a quiet port, rising
with occupancy and tripled above 70%. Dues accrue pro rata while a ship is berthed (at least
6 game hours a stay; the roadstead is free) and are settled, at the occupancy then, when it
leaves the berth and in the daily upkeep pass, from the owner's vault in this port's banking
region to its Crown.

coffee_house_gossip.description:
Coffee House gossip board: what ships saw on other ports' quays (stock, best bid and ask),
each port's report with its `snapshot_at`/`age_seconds`; a newer report of a port replaces
an older one. `null` below quay-tier visibility.

counting_house_min_lease_tons.description: Smallest single-company lease (tons) that earns counting-house visibility here.

effective_berths.description:
Berths now (see [`PortCatalogEntry::effective_berths`]); `occupied_berths` can exceed it
briefly after the fleet shrinks (berthed ships are never evicted by a shrink).

recent_sailings.description:
Ships seen sailing from or entering this port in the last 24 game hours, newest first
(name, hull, owner, bound for / came from, coarse load state; never cargo or timings).
`null` below quay-tier visibility.

visibility.description: The viewer's visibility tier at this port (`none` when unauthenticated).

PortId.description: Validated canonical port identifier (`"london"`, `"amsterdam"`, etc.) backed by the static world catalog.

as_of.description:
When the prices were observed: the daily snapshot time for `storage` (`null` until the
port's first snapshot), the response time for live tiers.

visibility.description:
Visibility tier the data was cut to: `storage` (day-old top of book), `counting_house`
(live top of book) or `quay` (live top of book plus full depth).

PortVisibility.description:
What a company can see of (and do at) one port's market, from weakest to strongest.

Ordered: `None < Storage < CountingHouse < Quay`, so `visibility >= PortVisibility::Storage`
reads "may trade here".

PositivePence.description:
Strictly positive monetary amount in pence (`100 pence = 1 Crown`), bounded to `1..=MAX_POSITIVE_PENCE`.

Enforces at construction and deserialization time that the value is at least `1p` and at most
[`MAX_POSITIVE_PENCE`] (`1,000,000,000,000p`), preventing zero/negative prices or `i64` multiplication overflow.

PositiveTons.description:
Strictly positive physical tonnage in tons, bounded to `1..=MAX_TONS`.

Used for order quantities, cargo transfers, and futures contract sizes where `0` or negative tons are invalid.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 / RFC 7807 HTTP Problem Details payload (`Content-Type: application/problem+json`).

batch_index.description:
For batch endpoints: zero-based index (in request order) of the item that failed.
Batches are atomic, so when this is present no item of the batch was applied.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.

oneOf.description: For `exceeds_insurable_value`: the most this ship can be insured for right now.
For `insufficient_provisions`: how many tons the ship's stores must hold to reach port fed.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type (e.g. `"Conflict"`).

type.description: URI reference identifying the problem type (e.g. `"urn:tradewinds:error:conflict"`).

source.description:
Where the provisions come from. To buy them on the market straight into the stores, place
an IOC bid with `into_stores: true` (POST /v1/market/order) instead.

ProvisionsShortfall.description: Why a departure was refused for want of provisions.

buy_provisions_tons.description: Whole tons to buy into the stores to cover the shortfall (rounded up).

required_provisions_tons.description:
Least provisions (tons, in total, fractional) the ship's stores must hold to keep the crew
fed to the destination with the current cargo aboard, assuming no hazards.

starving_leg_idx.description: First route leg the ship would set out on unfed.

stores_provisions_tons.description:
Provisions in the ship's stores now (tons, fractional; provisions carried as cargo do not
feed the crew).

PublicCompanyProfile.description: What anyone may see of a company.

leaderboard_rank.description:
Its place on the public leaderboard, when it is a player's ranked company in the top
[`LEADERBOARD_SIZE`].

titles.description: Hall-of-fame titles, shown on the owner's flagship company only.

expected_provisions_tons.description:
Least provisions (tons, fractional) in its stores that keep a lone ship of `ship_class` fed
to `to_port` whatever its cargo (each leg costed at the fully laden speed), with no
hazards: the crew eats exactly a ton per 100 crew-days and the stores run dry when they
reach 0, so this is what is eaten before the last leg sets out, plus a crumb. Compare it
with the ship's `stores.provisions_tons` and buy the difference rounded up to whole tons.

port_provisions_tons_per_day.description:
Tons of stores a `ship_class` crew eats per game day in port (berthed or in the roadstead):
half the sea rate of one ton per 100 crew-days (the crew eats partly ashore), eaten exactly.
Budget it for turnaround, convoy musters and idle days.

safe_provisions_tons.description:
`expected_provisions_tons` plus margin to stay fed after one storm or pirate attack takes a
quarter of the stores on any leg.

SailingDirection.description: Which way a notice's ship was moving.

SailingNotice.description: One public notice: a ship seen leaving or entering a port.

convoy_name.description: Name of the convoy it sails in, if any.

oneOf.description: Where it is bound (`sailed`) or came from (`arrived`).

port_id.description: The port where it was seen.

SeaZoneId.description: Validated canonical sea zone identifier (`"english_channel"`, `"north_sea"`, etc.) with hazard rates in `bps` (`10,000 bps = 100%`).

SeaZonePiracyResult.description:
A sea zone's live piracy (`GET /v1/world/zones`): the catalog rating, the summed letters of
marque and naval patrols in force (each capped per zone; every company's contributions stack),
and the net piracy every ship there sails through and Lloyd's prices. Aggregates only: sponsors
are anonymous.

marque_piracy_bps.description:
Piracy added by unexpired letters of marque (player-sponsored, corsair flotillas and
mutineers alike), capped at `5,000 bps`.

net_piracy_bps.description: `max(0, base + marque - patrol)`: the zone piracy the voyage hazard and Lloyd's use.

patrol_suppression_bps.description: Piracy suppressed by unexpired Crown Naval Patrols, capped at `5,000 bps`.

Season.description: Meteorological season of the in-game year, governing seasonal wind and storm patterns.

claim_pence.description: The rest of the adverse move, owed to the counterparty as a [`FuturesClaim`].

penalty_paid_pence.description:
What the defaulter paid at default: its forfeited margin plus as much of the adverse move as
its vault in the contract's region held.

stores_provisions_units.description:
Provisions in the ship's stores, in units of 1/10,000 crew-day
([`crate::catalog::PROVISION_UNITS_PER_TON`] a ton): what the crew eats, exactly. Not cargo,
but they take hold space (the whole tons they start) and count toward the ship's load.

ShipCargoItem.description: Single commodity line item in a ship's cargo hold, measured in positive metric `tons`.

ShipClassId.description: Validated canonical ship class identifier (`"hoy"`, `"fluyt"`, etc.) with speeds in `centiknots` (`100 centiknots = 1 knot`) and capacities in `tons`.

cargo_manifest.description: Cargo aboard (trade goods, provisions carried as goods included, and sealed freight).

effective_hold_capacity_tons.description: Cargo the ship can carry: the hold less mounted cannons (2 t each) and its stores.

stores.description: What the crew eats. Not cargo: stores take hold space but are never traded or delivered.

oneOf.description:
While sailing (solo or in convoy): the leg under way and the estimated arrival, at the
current speed (see [`VoyageEstimate`]); `null` otherwise.

ShipStatus.description: Operational lifecycle state of a vessel.

ShipStores.description:
A ship's stores: what its crew lives on. Stores take hold space (so they cut the cargo a ship
can load) and weigh the ship down, but they are not cargo: they cannot be sold, delivered or
carried as freight, and they are not insured cargo.

provisions_tons.description:
Provisions the crew eats, in tons (fractional: the stores are kept exactly). A ton feeds
100 crew-days at sea (eaten exactly, per leg), and in port half that, a ton per 200
crew-days (a hoy's ten hands a ton every twenty days). They take the whole tons they
start in the hold.

sea_days_remaining.description: Game days at sea these stores feed the ship's crew.

SimJobStatus.description: Execution state of an asynchronous simulation job in the event queue.

StoresCounterpart.description: Where provisions moved into or out of a ship's stores come from or go to.

effective_hold_capacity_tons.description: Cargo capacity left after the transfer (hold less cannons and stores).

turnaround_unlocks_at.description: Set when the transfer crossed the quay (warehouse), which extends the stevedore turnaround.

StreamAuthEnded.description: Data of an SSE `auth_revoked` / `auth_expired` event, sent right before the stream ends.

StreamGap.description: Data of an SSE `gap` event: events may have been missed and the client should resync via REST.

last_event_id.description: The resume id that could not be found.

reason.description:
`unknown_last_event_id`: the resume id is not in the event log (pruned past retention,
or never existed).

TimeInForce.description: Execution time-in-force policy for a spot market order.

Tons.description: Signed physical weight or capacity denominated in metric tons (`1 ton = 1 hold capacity unit`).

TopOfBookLevelResult.description: Best price on one side of a book and the total remaining size resting at that price.

destination.description: Where the provisions taken out of the stores go.

UpdateCompanySettingsRequest.description:
Partial update for [`CompanySettings`]: only the fields present change. Unknown fields are
rejected, so a misspelt preference is an error rather than a silent no-op.

VoyageEstimate.description:
Estimated schedule of the rest of a voyage. An estimate, not a promise: it assumes no hazard
strikes and that each leg starts the moment the previous one ends. It already accounts for
load changes from stores eaten en route and for starvation (speed halved once the stores
run out); cargo lost to storm or pirates, a convoy losing its slowest member, a late sim worker
and a berth queue at the destination (arrival there can mean anchoring in the roadstead) are
not foreseen.

current_leg_idx.description: Index into the route of the leg under way (or, before departure, the first leg).

estimated_arrival_at.description: Estimated arrival at the destination port (the last leg's estimate).

speed_centiknots.description: Speed of the leg under way.

locked_quantity.description: Tons reserved by open inventory locks (resting asks, listed freight contracts).

paused.description:
The server operators have paused the world: game time stands still (`calendar` is frozen),
nothing at sea moves, and mutating requests answer `503 world_paused` until it resumes.

WorldEventResult.description:
A world event as published: what happened where, in words. Never carries magnitudes or hidden
economy parameters (tonnages, rate factors, durations of structural shifts).

added_piracy_bps.description: Piracy added in the sea zone (`pirate_outbreak`).

charter_id.description:
The public charter the event spawned (`admiralty_mobilization`; a `demand_shortage` crisis
charter is local news, listed only on its quay or as gossip).

expires_at.description: When the event (for a structural shift: the news of it) lapses. Not the end of a shift.

is_active.description: Still in effect (`expires_at` in the future).

structural.description: A structural shift: a lasting change to a port's economy (how large or how long is not said).

WorldEventType.description: Kind of a world event: one of the director's macro shocks, or a structural shift (§3.1a).
